shapes.name: The reveal (open loop and clues)
shapes.when: how a business really makes money, a secret of the rich, a billionaire question: there is one hidden answer
shapes.beats: hook: the surprising fact and the question, no answer -> promise ('here's how') -> clue one, clue two, clue three, each a bigger piece -> the turn (the piece nobody expects) -> the payoff answers the hook in one line

reference.title: Why does the casino always win, even when nobody cheats? | How Casinos Make Money

shapes.name: Versus
shapes.when: two people or two choices in the same situation, one difference that decides everything
shapes.beats: hook: the same moment, two outcomes -> promise ('one choice decides it') -> side by side: what each does, step by step, the gap widening -> the turn (the real reason) -> the payoff

reference.title: rich vs poor parents buying you a car

shapes.name: Countdown
shapes.when: a handful of things of one kind (tricks, traps, ways): number three, two, then the biggest
shapes.beats: hook: the biggest one teased, not shown -> promise ('three ways, the last is the worst') -> three, two -> the turn -> number one, the payoff

reference.title: 6 Ways Rich People Make Money With Debt

shapes.name: Before and after
shapes.when: one change and what it did: a decision, a law, a company's move, a fortune over time
shapes.beats: hook: the after, shocking, with the question how -> the before, in enough detail to matter -> the change -> what happened step by step -> the turn -> the payoff (the after, explained)

reference.title: Everyone Called Him an Idiot. He Got Richer Every Time.

shapes.name: Then and now
shapes.when: how something changed across years: a price, a fortune, an industry, who was the first billionaire of it
shapes.beats: hook: today's figure next to the old one, and why -> the start -> two or three moments that changed it, in order -> the turn -> today, explained

reference.title: Who Was The 1st Billionaire In These Industries?!

shapes.name: What if
shapes.when: an imagined scenario at a scale people can't picture: spend $1 trillion in a day, pay off the national debt, give everyone a billion
shapes.beats: hook: the wild question -> the rules of the game -> try it, step by step, the number growing -> the turn (where it breaks) -> the payoff (what it teaches)

reference.title: I Tried to Spend $1 TRILLION in One Day

shapes.name: The question chain (asker and explainer)
shapes.when: a billionaire or big-money mechanism with several layers: how the rich pay no tax, how a company really earns, why a famous person does something strange
shapes.beats: hook: the asker states the shocking fact and asks why -> the explainer answers in one line and one picture -> the asker's next, sharper question (doubt, then how, then a real example, then outrage, then 'and people like us?') -> each answer a real name and a figure, a named term on a card -> the named secret -> a 3-line recap, the lesson, the asker's last question to the viewer

reference.title: Why Billionaires Take $0 Salary… But Never Go Broke

shapes.name: The ladder parable (same start, different steps)
shapes.when: one money idea shown as people climbing it: same $100, four brothers; same salary, three friends. Each step a named finance term, the result multiplied at every step
shapes.beats: hook: the same start and the wildly different end -> the cast in a lineup -> person one: the simplest move, the sum built on screen from units, its term -> person two, three, four: each one more clever move, a small conflict (who pays if it fails?) and how it's solved, the sum and the term -> the bars side by side -> the 3-line contrast recap -> 'which one are you?'

reference.title: How $100 Became $204,984: The Egg Selling Mindset

shapes.name: The true rise (and the hits)
shapes.when: how a real company, person or place got rich: a founding sum, dated steps, a crisis, the comeback
shapes.beats: hook: the question written huge over today's picture ('why is X so rich?') -> rewind to the start with its date and sum -> growth you can count (stores, customers, ships) -> 'but then' the dated setbacks -> the comeback -> the lesson and a question to the viewer

reference.title: Why Are Dubai Locals So Rich? (It's Not Oil)

shapes.name: The zoom-in
shapes.when: a famous total too big to picture, made real by dividing it down to one night and one person; fits tours, stadiums, launches, sales days
shapes.beats: hook: the giant total with the famous name, as one striking rate -> promise: how can it be that much? -> how the money is really made, one step a beat (who pays, for what, the rule behind it) -> the turn: the part people miss (what the total is NOT, or who really pays) -> payoff: the most surprising slice, and a question. One time rate at most: never the same total per hour, per day, per year
shapes.revised: 2026-11-14: owner note on v-20261114-03, the unit ladder (minute, hour, day, year) gave the viewer nothing they didn't know

shapes.name: Follow the flow
shapes.when: a machine explainer is one journey through its parts; the reveal shape is blocked and none of the others is a journey
shapes.beats: hook: the machine running and the question -> follow one thing (water, a signal) through each stage on a glowing path -> the key part, opened -> the number that makes it work -> the turn: what happens when the input weakens -> payoff: the most surprising figure -> loop to the first frame

shapes.name: Build it, then dive
shapes.when: an invention whose one part became billions: build the original, then dive into today's chip; reveal and follow-the-flow are blocked
shapes.beats: hook: today's chip and the question -> the first one built part by part in 3D -> how it works, the causal step shown -> the proof it worked -> the scale dive from that one switch down into a modern chip -> payoff: the most surprising figure -> loop to the chip in your hand

shapes.name: From a small thing to the giant machine
shapes.when: a big machine whose one principle the viewer already knows from a small everyday thing (a hamster wheel and a power plant, a bicycle pump and a jet engine); the scale steps are real machines, never invented ones
shapes.beats: hook: the small thing in the hand and the giant one behind it, the question -> the principle shown on the small thing -> step up: the same principle in a bigger real machine, one scale a beat -> the turn: the step where size breaks the simple version and needs a new trick -> payoff: the giant machine with its most surprising sourced figure -> loop back to the small thing

reference.title: How a Stack of Bricks Becomes a Skyscraper

shapes.note: Technique only: never their words, titles or art. Their channel runs every video as an everyday-object-to-giant ladder, 100-130 s each.

shapes.name: Nose to tail
shapes.when: a long machine is best explained by travelling along it from the front to the back; reveal, follow-the-flow and build-and-dive are blocked
shapes.beats: hook: the city's ground sliced open, old tunnels and the machine coming -> promise: how it gets through -> the machine's size -> walk it from the cutting face back, one part a beat (cutterhead, pressure chamber, conveyor, ring builder) -> the turn: the Tube tunnel right beside it -> payoff: the smallest gap -> loop to the first frame
